editorial_intro: The Bear wraps up on JioHotstar, Rajamouli revisits Baahubali's legacy on Netflix, and a fresh batch of Korean thrillers rounds out a stacked weekend.

picks.title: Baahubali: The Torchbearer
picks.synopsis: A four-part documentary revisiting the Baahubali saga a decade on. SS Rajamouli, Prabhas, and Rana Daggubati open up about the creative vision, production hurdles, and financial gambles behind India's biggest film franchise.
picks.why_watch: Essential viewing if you've ever wondered how two Telugu films rewrote Indian cinema's rulebook.

picks.title: Perfect Family
picks.synopsis: The Karkarias look picture-perfect until their youngest daughter's anxiety sends the whole family into therapy. Buried resentments, unspoken guilt, and long-dodged conversations spill out — sometimes hilariously, sometimes painfully.
picks.why_watch: Gulshan Devaiah + Manoj Pahwa in a family therapy comedy? That casting alone is worth the click.

picks.title: Alliance
picks.synopsis: Kunal Kemmu hosts 16 contestants who are paired up and tested through shifting alliances, betrayals, and strategic gameplay. Think Survivor meets Indian social dynamics.
picks.why_watch: India's answer to the strategy-reality genre — Kunal Kemmu brings the right energy as host.

picks.title: The Bear: Season 5 (Final)
picks.synopsis: Carmy and his crew return for the final season. The kitchen's running, the restaurant's got a rep, but personal stakes have never been higher. Jeremy Allen White delivers one last masterclass in controlled chaos.
picks.why_watch: The last supper. If you've been riding with Carmy since Season 1, clear your Friday night.

picks.title: Avatar: The Last Airbender — Season 2
picks.synopsis: The live-action adaptation continues as Aang, Katara, and Sokka push deeper into the Earth Kingdom. Bigger bending, bigger battles, and Toph is finally here.
picks.why_watch: Season 1 proved the live-action could work. Season 2 brings Toph — the fandom's been waiting.

picks.title: Little Brother
picks.synopsis: A buttoned-up real estate agent's life goes sideways when his former 'little brother' from a mentorship program shows up unannounced and refuses to leave. John Cena and Eric André are a surprisingly great odd couple.
picks.why_watch: Eric André bringing chaos into John Cena's structured life is exactly the comedy setup that writes itself.

picks.title: Notes from the Last Row
picks.synopsis: A literature professor discovers raw talent in a quiet student's writing — then gets drawn dangerously deep into the student's stories, which blur the line between fiction and voyeurism. Based on the Spanish play The Boy in the Last Row.
picks.why_watch: Choi Min-sik (Oldboy) in a psychological cat-and-mouse with K-drama's hottest rising star? Yes please.

picks.title: Agent Kim Reactivated
picks.synopsis: A retired black-ops agent has built a quiet life as a single dad. When his daughter is kidnapped, he's pulled back into the world he thought he'd left behind. Classic revenge-action done Korean-style.
picks.why_watch: Taken meets Korean action cinema. If you like John Wick energy with a dad-mode twist, this is your weekend pick.

picks.title: Undertone
picks.synopsis: An A24 supernatural horror hitting streaming. A slow-burn descent into dread set in a remote community where something ancient is stirring beneath the surface.
picks.why_watch: A24 horror on Max — if you trust the A24 label for elevated scares, give this a Friday night shot.

picks.title: Life, Larry and the Pursuit of Unhappiness
picks.synopsis: HBO's latest comedy series — a curmudgeonly protagonist navigates modern life's absurdities with the kind of brutal honesty that makes you laugh and cringe in equal measure.
picks.why_watch: If you miss Curb Your Enthusiasm, HBO might have just given you a spiritual successor.
